title: Normalized multiplication of support quotient sheaves on products
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ for its open complement and set
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad \tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^\tau_{T,C}$. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Z\hookrightarrow X$, $W\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P=X\times_kY$, $S=Z\times_kW$, with projections $p_X,p_Y$ [def-pc-base-change]. In each topology multiplication of quotient generators specifies an isomorphism
$$e_\tau:p_X^*Q^\tau_{X,Z}\otimes_A p_Y^*Q^\tau_{Y,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^\tau_{P,S},\qquad \overline a\otimes\overline b\longmapsto\overline{ab}.$$
Here tensor is the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and pullback uses the constant coefficient inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The same map is an isomorphism for derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor]. The maps $e_\tau$ are natural for maps of the two pairs of schemes and closed supports inducing the pullbacks in this formula.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: multiplication of quotient generators identifies the product support quotient, with the etale and pro-etale normalizations.

proof.text: Identify each recorded cokernel Q_a with a_* of the constant coefficient unit, normalized on the quotient generator. Closed restriction kills the open extension term, so it makes the cokernel projection invertible. Open restriction makes the defining counit invertible and hence kills its cokernel; it also kills the closed direct image. The inverse-image/direct-image unit is invertible after closed restriction by the fully faithful counit and the triangle identity. The cokernel descendent to a_* of the constant unit is therefore an isomorphism by open/closed conservativity. For pro-etale sheaves use the fixed-scalar open/closed detection theorem; derive closed restriction of extension by zero vanishing from the two adjunctions and open restriction of closed direct image vanishing. Finite type over the field makes X, Y and P locally Noetherian, giving quasi-compact open complements.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: multiplication of quotient generators identifies the product support quotient, with the etale and pro-etale normalizations.

proof.text: Apply the existing uniquely normalized supported-coefficient tensor comparison at the two coefficient units. Compose with the inverse unit isomorphism on coefficients and the three normalized cokernel identifications from step 1. This constructs b: Q_product -> p_X^*Q_i tensor p_Y^*Q_j with r_product followed by b equal to the recorded product generator m. Naturality of the coefficient quotient in a coefficient-module map proves this normalization exactly. Constant exterior tensor is invertible: its presheaf pairing has identity components, sheafification is monoidal, and both inverse-image identifications of constant sheaves are invertible. Each quotient projection, its inverse image and their tensor are epic; hence m and then b are epic.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: multiplication of quotient generators identifies the product support quotient, with the etale and pro-etale normalizations.

proof.text: The composite of the product-support immersion with each ambient projection factors through the corresponding closed immersion. Inverse-image composition transports the closed-restriction isomorphisms of the two quotient projections to the product support. Strong monoidality of inverse image then makes the restriction of m invertible. Since the restriction of r_product is invertible by step 1, the normalization r_product b = m makes the closed restriction of b invertible. On the complementary open, the source of b is zero by step 1, so epicness makes its target zero too. Open/closed conservativity now makes b invertible in each topology. Take e=b^{-1}; the same normalization gives m e = r_product.

proof.text: Recover ordinary categorical flatness of the etale quotient from its normalized geometric fibers in the quotient-flat lemma, using the source flatness criterion; obtain pro-etale flatness from its normalized comparison with the etale quotient and flatness of comparison inverse image. Projection inverse image preserves flatness, in the finite-coefficient pro-etale case because the ring is Noetherian. A flat object in degree zero is K-flat. The source K-flat localization theorem makes the lax monoidal map of Qh invertible and hence that of Q invertible via quotientCompQhIso. The supported-derived localization comparison is this map followed by Q of an equality isomorphism, so it too is invertible.

proof.text: For uniqueness, cancel the epic product generator from the two normalization equations and apply Iso.ext. For the stated naturality predicate, apply h^* to the normalization equation and cancel the still-epic h^*m. The two generator-preserving equations in the predicate then reduce the desired square to the normalization equation on the new base. This proves exactly the quantified predicate, for every h and every compatible pair of generator-preserving maps in either topology.
